To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Bayesian inference is a promising direction for improving deep neural networks and that the current state of the art is not sufficient.

(1) Bayesian inference for large scale image classification can be performed efficiently, (2) Bayesian neural networks can outperform their non-Bayesian counterparts in terms of accuracy, (3) Bayesian neural networks are robust to overfit, (4) Bayesian neural networks provide a calibrated measure for uncertainty that can be used to improve the decision making process, and (5) Bayesian neural networks have a smaller number of hyperparameters than their non-Bayesain counterparts

(a) Bayesian neural network training is not only theoretically sound, but also practically feasible for large-scale image classification, and that (b) Bayesian neural network inference can be performed at test time in a computationally tractable manner that is compatible with modern deep learning architectures and hardware.
